text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Jordanian press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- King Hussein's coming talks with U.S. President Clinton in Washington are expected to focus on an Israeli drive to expand Jewish settlements in Palestinian territories.
- Jordan's Engineers Union plan to stage a sit-in near the prime ministry on Saturday over the government's continued reluctance to meet their pay demands.
- Jordan's prominent public figures continue to voice their condemnation and rejection of an Israeli decision to build a settlement on the Jabal Abu Ghuneim area in Arab East Jerusalem.

- During a visit to Al-Hussein orphanage accompanied by Queen Noor, king is briefed on the social circumstances of orphans and homeless children; he emphasises the need to ensure a decent living for them.
- Prime Minister Kabariti condemns the construction of the new Jewish settlement in Abu Ghuneim; says the Israeli decision is "very serious and very damaging and threatens Middle East peace".
- Thirty-seven kgs of hashish and 1,850 cartons of smuggled cigarettes seized by customs officials from the border posts with Iraq and Syria during last week.
